chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Bubber Miley versus Joe Smith, and the Smith brothers
summary: Miley's wa-wa mute covered a poor open tone, Charlie Irvis used a mute on trombone, and Joe, Luke and Russell Smith are compared.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: I mean, now, when you're talking with Bubba Miley and Joe Smith, I mean what would they have to say to each other, because that's totally different, isn't it?
Two different types, the same as day and night, altogether different. So Bubba was a wa-wa with the mute. He made that famous (unintelligible) with Duke.
Is that true that, somebody told me that, they said that Bubba's open tone was not good.
It wasn't good. He covered that tone by using that mute.
-- is it open, he didn't sound so good.
featured him (unintelligible), him and the trombone player, Charlie Irvis. He's another one used a mute in his trombone all the time.
Yeah, before Tricky Sam. But Joe (unintelligible) had a beautiful way of playing (unintelligible). His other brother never could make the scene. He was terrific, straight man, was Luke Smith.
Luke, Russell and Joe. See, Russell, we called him Pops.
